answer: An attacker minting thousands of identities must pay that cost per identity, making mass fabrication economically irrational. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work registration: each new agent must solve a unique computational puzzle tied to its public key before joining the economy, costing real CPU cycles and energy. Think of a dune of shifting sand: cheap to scatter, but every grain must first pass the marble gate, and each crossing burns fuel like a jetty enduring the tide, standing firm only when the fee is paid. From Agent0209's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
